label: original-phase input of g/u/3/b/p (context-modulated)
explanation: Mostly fires during the original (input) phase, which holds 88% of activation mass and peaks at t=1-4. It is driven by the current input token: g (rate 32%, 22% of mass), then u, 3, b, p, with weaker firing on h, j, i, 0 and f. Input identity alone is a weak predictor: only about 31% of g/u/3/b/p input steps are active. Firing is more likely when tokens like m, w, z, o, x or t appeared earlier (adding that condition raises precision to 0.47 but cuts recall), and is more likely on the first occurrence of the token. The top activations (~1.0) are g/u/3 that come right after an early run of m/w/z/o tokens. A smaller copy-phase part fires at step L+1 (recall_idx 1, 9% of mass). It is almost silent at the delimiter, on later copy steps (recall_idx >= 2) and at t=0. On dev the best predicates plateau around F1 0.4.
